title: Does the best AI model's lead come from quantization, or the model?
summary: Eleven single-model setups, each making a fast Answer plus a separate In-Depth explanation (both graded): five model families tested at both 8-bit and 4-bit precision — Google Gemma 4 12B, Alibaba Qwen 3 14B, Qwen 2.5 14B, IBM Granite 3.3 8B, and Mistral NeMo 12B — plus a reasoning model (Qwen 3.6 35B). 32 clinical questions across three patients, judged against the full chart on two independent axes.
takeaway: Gemma 4 12B tops both axes (Answer 75.8, In-Depth 65.7) — and its lead is not a precision artifact: Gemma at 4-bit matched (and slightly edged) Gemma at 8-bit, while quantization moved the other models inconsistently and mostly within noise. Mistral NeMo was the weakest clinical reader (55.8 at 8-bit, 7 unsafe answers). Grading the separate In-Depth explanation exposed safety failures the short Answer hides — Granite 4-bit's In-Depth produced 12 unsafe elaborations and Mistral 8-bit's produced 8. The reasoning model (Qwen 3.6 35B) was safe but did not top Gemma 12B.
